library(MASS)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +

tech <- readRDS("../data/processed/tech_clean.rds")

\newpage

# 1. Model Data

## Overlapping Features

```{r exact-overlap}
# Exact overlaps: these add up to 1 for every article
all(abs(tech$rate_positive_words + tech$rate_negative_words - 1) < 1e-9)
all(abs(tech$LDA_00 + tech$LDA_01 + tech$LDA_02 + tech$LDA_03 + tech$LDA_04 - 1) < 1e-6)
```

* `rate_negative_words` is exactly 1 minus `rate_positive_words`
* `LDA_04` is exactly 1 minus the other four topic scores
* Keeping all of them would make the model unsolvable (exact collinearity)

```{r near-overlap}
overlap_pairs <- data.frame(
  dropped = c("n_unique_tokens", "self_reference_min_shares", "self_reference_max_shares",
              "kw_max_avg"),
  kept    = c("n_non_stop_unique_tokens", "self_reference_avg_shares",
              "self_reference_avg_shares", "kw_avg_avg")
)

overlap_pairs$correlation <- round(mapply(function(a, b) cor(tech[[a]], tech[[b]]),
                                          overlap_pairs$dropped, overlap_pairs$kept), 2)
knitr::kable(overlap_pairs, row.names = FALSE)
```

* Each dropped column has a correlation of 0.75 to 0.93 with the one we keep

```{r vif-before}
# VIF with every candidate count, rate and popularity feature
candidates <- tech |>
  select(n_tokens_content, num_hrefs, num_self_hrefs, n_unique_tokens,
         n_non_stop_unique_tokens, global_sentiment_polarity,
         global_rate_positive_words, global_rate_negative_words, rate_positive_words,
         kw_min_min, kw_max_min, kw_avg_min, kw_min_max, kw_max_max, kw_avg_max,
         kw_min_avg, kw_max_avg, kw_avg_avg, self_reference_min_shares,
         self_reference_max_shares, self_reference_avg_shares)

round(sort(vif(candidates), decreasing = TRUE)[1:6], 1)
```

```{r vif-after}
kept <- tech |>
  select(n_tokens_content, num_hrefs, num_self_hrefs, n_non_stop_unique_tokens,
         global_sentiment_polarity, global_rate_positive_words,
         global_rate_negative_words, kw_avg_avg, self_reference_avg_shares)

round(sort(vif(kept), decreasing = TRUE), 1)
```

* Before dropping, five features have VIF above 10. The highest is
  `self_reference_avg_shares` (28.6), because its min and max versions are also in
* After dropping, every VIF is 2.3 or lower
* The nine `kw_` columns are all summaries of keyword popularity, and the min
  columns are full of `-1` and `0` placeholders. We keep only `kw_avg_avg`, the
  average keyword's average shares, as one clear measure

\newpage

## Features Used

```{r model-data}
model_data <- tech |>
  mutate(
    log_words      = log1p(n_tokens_content),
    log_hrefs      = log1p(num_hrefs),
    log_self_hrefs = log1p(num_self_hrefs),
    log_kw_avg_avg = log1p(kw_avg_avg),
    log_self_ref   = log1p(self_reference_avg_shares),
    quarter        = factor(quarter)
  )

controllable <- c("weekend", "vid_group", "img_group", "log_words", "n_tokens_title",
                  "log_hrefs", "log_self_hrefs", "num_keywords", "average_token_length",
                  "n_non_stop_unique_tokens", "global_sentiment_polarity",
                  "global_subjectivity", "global_rate_positive_words",
                  "global_rate_negative_words", "avg_positive_polarity",
                  "avg_negative_polarity", "title_sentiment_polarity", "title_subjectivity")

uncontrollable <- c("log_kw_avg_avg", "log_self_ref", "LDA_00", "LDA_01", "LDA_02", "LDA_03",
             "quarter")

features <- paste(c(controllable, uncontrollable), collapse = " + ")
```

* Controllable features: things an editor chooses (day, visuals, length, links,
  wording, tone)
* Uncontrollable features: things an editor can't directly change (topic popularity,
  popularity of linked articles, topic, time period)
* Skewed counts use `log(x + 1)`
* `quarter` replaces `timedelta` to account for drift over time
* Dropped for overlapping with a kept feature (see Overlapping Features above)

\newpage

# 2. Full Linear Model

## Response Transformation

```{r boxcox}
g_raw <- lm(as.formula(paste("shares ~", features)), data = model_data)
bc <- boxcox(g_raw, lambda = seq(-1, 1, by = 0.01))

bc$x[which.max(bc$y)]
range(bc$x[bc$y > max(bc$y) - qchisq(0.95, 1) / 2])
```

* Box-Cox picks $\lambda \approx -0.24$, far from 1, so raw shares need a transformation
* We use log shares ($\lambda = 0$) instead. It's close to the best $\lambda$ and
  each coefficient reads as a percent change in shares

## Weekday vs Weekend

```{r day-vs-weekend}
g_full <- lm(as.formula(paste("log_shares ~", features)), data = model_data)
g_day  <- update(g_full, . ~ . - weekend + weekday)

anova_tab <- anova(g_full, g_day)
rownames(anova_tab) <- c("Weekday vs weekend", "7 days")
knitr::kable(anova_tab, digits = 3)
```

* $H_0$: the six extra day terms are 0 (weekday vs weekend is enough)
* p = 0.12, so we fail to reject and keep weekday vs weekend

## Collinearity

```{r vif}
round(sort(vif(g_full), decreasing = TRUE)[1:6], 2)
```

* All VIFs are under 10, so collinearity isn't a problem
* The highest is article tone (6.07), since the positive and negative word rates
  partly measure the same thing

\newpage

## Diagnostics

```{r diagnostics, fig.height = 6}
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(g_full)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

* Residuals vs Fitted: centered on 0 with no clear curve
* Q-Q: heavy upper tail from a few viral articles
* Scale-Location: close to flat
* Residuals vs Leverage: no points past the Cook's distance lines

```{r bp-test}
bptest(g_full)
```

* $H_0$: constant error variance. p < 0.001, so we reject
* With 7,325 articles, the test picks up small differences in spread
* Coefficient estimates are still unbiased, but p-values may be a little too
  small.

\newpage

## Unusual Points

```{r leverage}
n <- nrow(model_data)
p <- length(coef(g_full))

lev <- hatvalues(g_full)
sum(lev > 2 * p / n)

jack <- rstudent(g_full)
sum(abs(jack) > abs(qt(0.05 / (2 * n), n - p - 1)))  # Bonferroni

cook <- cooks.distance(g_full)
max(cook)
```

```{r cooks, fig.height = 3.5}
halfnorm(cook, 3, ylab = "Cook's distances")
```

* 147 articles have high leverage ($h_i > 2p/n$), 2% of the data
* 5 articles are outliers after the Bonferroni correction, all viral articles
  with far more shares than predicted
* Largest Cook's distance is 0.011, far below 1, so no single article changes
  the fit. We keep all articles

\newpage

# 3. Variable Selection

```{r step}
g_aic <- step(g_full, direction = "backward", trace = 0)
g_bic <- step(g_full, direction = "backward", k = log(n), trace = 0)

all_terms <- c(controllable, uncontrollable)

data.frame(
  feature = all_terms,
  group   = ifelse(all_terms %in% controllable, "Controllable", "Uncontrollable"),
  AIC     = ifelse(all_terms %in% attr(terms(g_aic), "term.labels"), "Kept", ""),
  BIC     = ifelse(all_terms %in% attr(terms(g_bic), "term.labels"), "Kept", "")
) |> knitr::kable(row.names = FALSE)
```

* Backward elimination, starting from the full model
* AIC drops 7 features. BIC drops 14, since it penalizes extra terms more
* Both keep weekend, videos, word count, links, links, article tone,
  subjectivity, headline tone, keyword popularity, linked-article popularity
  and quarter
* BIC also drops images, title length, number of keywords, word variety, the
  other sentiment measures and the topic scores

```{r model-compare}
data.frame(
  model    = c("Full", "AIC", "BIC"),
  terms    = c(length(coef(g_full)), length(coef(g_aic)), length(coef(g_bic))) - 1,
  adj_r2   = round(c(summary(g_full)$adj.r.squared, summary(g_aic)$adj.r.squared,
                     summary(g_bic)$adj.r.squared), 4),
  AIC      = round(c(AIC(g_full), AIC(g_aic), AIC(g_bic))),
  BIC      = round(c(BIC(g_full), BIC(g_aic), BIC(g_bic)))
) |> knitr::kable(row.names = FALSE)
```

* Adjusted $R^2$ barely changes (0.085 to 0.083), so the dropped features add
  almost nothing
* We use the BIC model as the final model since it's the simplest

## Final Model

```{r final}
knitr::kable(summary(g_bic)$coefficients, digits = 4)
summary(g_bic)$r.squared
```

* Every remaining term is significant at 0.01
* The final model explains about 8.5% of the variation in log shares

\newpage

# 4. Random Forest

```{r rf}
set.seed(443)
train_rows <- sample(n, round(0.8 * n))
train <- model_data[train_rows, ]
test  <- model_data[-train_rows, ]

rf <- randomForest(as.formula(paste("log_shares ~", features)),
                   data = train, ntree = 300, importance = TRUE)

lm_full_train <- update(g_full, data = train)
lm_bic_train  <- update(g_bic, data = train)
```

* The forest uses every feature, since it doesn't need variable selection

## Accuracy on Test Articles

```{r accuracy}
test_r2 <- function(pred) {
  1 - sum((test$log_shares - pred)^2) / sum((test$log_shares - mean(test$log_shares))^2)
}

data.frame(
  model   = c("Full linear", "BIC linear", "Random forest"),
  test_r2 = round(c(test_r2(predict(lm_full_train, test)),
                    test_r2(predict(lm_bic_train, test)),
                    test_r2(predict(rf, test))), 3)
) |> knitr::kable(row.names = FALSE)
```

* The forest explains more on new articles (about 14% vs 8%), since it picks
  up curves and combinations of features
* The BIC model does as well as the full model with far fewer terms

\newpage

# 5. What Drives Shares

```{r importance-data}
ranking <- data.frame(feature = rownames(importance(rf)),
                      importance = importance(rf)[, "%IncMSE"]) |>
  mutate(group = ifelse(feature %in% controllable, "Controllable", "Uncontrollable"))
```

* Importance = how much worse the forest's predictions get when a feature's
  values are shuffled

```{r importance-all, fig.height = 5}
ggplot(ranking, aes(importance, reorder(feature, importance))) +
  geom_col(fill = "grey45") +
  labs(x = "Increase in error when shuffled (%)", y = NULL,
       title = "Most important features for predicting shares")
```

* Keyword popularity, word count, weekend and links rank highest

```{r importance-controllable, fig.height = 4}
ranking |>
  filter(group == "Controllable") |>
  ggplot(aes(importance, reorder(feature, importance))) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(x = "Increase in error when shuffled (%)", y = NULL,
       title = "Most important features an author controls")
```

* Word count, weekend and links rank highest among controllable features
* Videos rank lower than their effect suggests because 72% of articles have
  none, so shuffling them changes few predictions

```{r importance-combined, fig.height = 5}
ggplot(ranking, aes(importance, reorder(feature, importance), fill = group)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Controllable = "steelblue", Uncontrollable = "grey65"),
                    name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Increase in error when shuffled (%)", y = NULL,
       title = "Feature importance by group") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```


```{r importance-plain, fig.height = 3.8, include=FALSE}
# Plain-language version of the importance chart for the progress report
plain <- c(
  log_kw_avg_avg = "Past popularity of keywords", log_words = "Word count",
  weekend = "Weekend vs weekday", log_hrefs = "Number of links",
  n_non_stop_unique_tokens = "Variety of words used",
  log_self_ref = "Popularity of linked site articles",
  log_self_hrefs = "Links to the site's own articles",
  global_sentiment_polarity = "Overall tone", quarter = "Time period",
  global_rate_positive_words = "Share of positive words", img_group = "Number of images",
  global_rate_negative_words = "Share of negative words", LDA_03 = "Topic group 4",
  num_keywords = "Number of keywords", vid_group = "Number of videos",
  LDA_01 = "Topic group 2", avg_negative_polarity = "Strength of negative words",
  avg_positive_polarity = "Strength of positive words",
  title_sentiment_polarity = "Headline tone", LDA_00 = "Topic group 1",
  global_subjectivity = "Amount of opinion", LDA_02 = "Topic group 3",
  average_token_length = "Average word length", title_subjectivity = "Headline opinion",
  n_tokens_title = "Headline length")

data.frame(feature = rownames(importance(rf)),
           importance = importance(rf)[, "%IncMSE"]) |>
  mutate(group = ifelse(feature %in% controllable, "Within the site's control",
                        "Topic and timing"),
         label = plain[feature]) |>
  arrange(desc(importance)) |>
  head(10) |>
  ggplot(aes(importance, reorder(label, importance), fill = group)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`Within the site's control` = "steelblue",
                               `Topic and timing` = "grey65"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "How much worse predictions get without this factor (%)", y = NULL,
       title = "Keyword popularity, length and weekend timing matter most",
       subtitle = "Top 10 factors in the random forest") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

* Forest importance and BIC selection mostly agree. The main exception is word
  variety (`n_non_stop_unique_tokens`), which ranks high in the forest but is
  dropped by BIC, likely because its effect isn't a straight line

\newpage

# 6. Interpretation

* Effects come from the final (BIC) model, holding every other feature fixed
* Since the response is log shares, a coefficient $\hat\beta$ means shares change
  by $100(e^{\hat\beta} - 1)\%$ for a one-unit increase
* For log features, doubling the count changes shares by $100(2^{\hat\beta} - 1)\%$
* For scores from 0 to 1, we use a 0.1 increase: $100(e^{0.1\hat\beta} - 1)\%$

```{r effects}
b <- coef(g_bic)

effects <- data.frame(
  change = c("Weekend instead of weekday", "1 video instead of none",
             "2+ videos instead of none", "Double the word count",
             "Double the links", "Double the links to other articles",
             "Article tone +0.1 (more positive)", "Subjectivity +0.1 (more opinion)",
             "Headline tone +0.1 (more positive)",
             "Double keyword popularity", "Double linked-article popularity"),
  group = c(rep("Controllable", 9), rep("Uncontrollable", 2)),
  pct_change = c(exp(b["weekendWeekend"]) - 1,
                 exp(b["vid_group1"]) - 1,
                 exp(b["vid_group2+"]) - 1,
                 2^b["log_words"] - 1,
                 2^b["log_hrefs"] - 1,
                 2^b["log_self_hrefs"] - 1,
                 exp(0.1 * b["global_sentiment_polarity"]) - 1,
                 exp(0.1 * b["global_subjectivity"]) - 1,
                 exp(0.1 * b["title_sentiment_polarity"]) - 1,
                 2^b["log_kw_avg_avg"] - 1,
                 2^b["log_self_ref"] - 1)
) |>
  mutate(pct_change = round(100 * pct_change, 1))

knitr::kable(effects, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r effects-chart, fig.height = 4}
effects |>
  filter(group == "Controllable") |>
  ggplot(aes(pct_change, reorder(change, pct_change))) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(pct_change, "%"),
                hjust = ifelse(pct_change > 0, -0.15, 1.15)), size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.25)) +
  labs(x = "Change in shares (%)", y = NULL,
       title = "Weekend posting and videos move shares the most")
```

* Posting on a weekend instead of a weekday: about 34% more shares
* One video: about 17% more shares. Two or more: about 30% more
* Doubling the word count: about 7% more. Doubling the links: about 8% more
* Doubling links to other articles: about 11% fewer
* A more positive article: slightly fewer shares. A more opinionated article or
  a more positive headline: slightly more
* Images aren't in the final model, so they don't affect shares once the other
  features are accounted for

## URL Date Check

```{r url-check}
g_url <- update(g_bic, . ~ . - weekend + url_is_weekend)
round(100 * (exp(coef(g_url)["url_is_weekend"]) - 1), 1)
```

* About a quarter of articles have a different weekday in the URL than in the data
* Using the URL date, the weekend effect is about 26% instead of 34%
* Smaller, but still the largest controllable effect
